AfterSideTurnStart.rationale: CLOSED 2026-07-28 (round 3) by the gap-queue continuation's post-section-A pass -- the turn-start split, the combat-over hook gate, Glass Eye's reward set, the out-of-combat potion action and the choose-a-card selector arm. This is a CODE change, not a re-reading of the old code. The phase collapse this entry was filed for is gone. `on_player_turn_started` served THREE distinct C# phases; it now serves exactly one (Hook.AfterPlayerTurnStart), with `after_side_turn_start` for :522 and `after_auto_pre_play_phase_entered` for the AutoPrePlay phase, dispatched in that order from PlayerCombatState.start_turn. ClarityPower.cs declares AfterSideTurnStart, so it is on the middle one. The Late sub-pass is already covered by HookSystem._each's suffix machinery (`after_side_turn_start_late` dispatches if any listener declares it).  The gap it replaced read: The SLOT is right and the group's usual slot gap does not apply here: Hook.AfterSideTurnStart (CombatManager.cs:522) is post-draw, and the sim's on_player_turn_started (player.py:186) is the post-draw slot -- confirmed by the ordering table in this record's source comments and by py audit/tools/power_census.py slots (which flags the unit only as NO-SIM-SIDE-START-SLOT, i.e. no side-scoped dispatch, not as a wrong slot). What IS a gap is the phase collapse: PHASE COLLAPSE. The sim's on_player_turn_started (player.py:186) is a single slot serving THREE distinct C# phases that the game runs in a fixed order: Hook.AfterPlayerTurnStart (CombatManager.cs:675, inside the SetupPlayerTurn task launched at :514), then Hook.AfterSideTurnStart (:522), then Hook.AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEntered (:568 -> RunAutoPrePlayPhase, :613-619). Collapsing them makes the relative order of this power and every other turn-start power a function of hook-REGISTRATION order, i.e. of which card the player happened to play first. Same shape as hook_dispatch's G3 (the Early/Late phase passes do not exist) one level up, and the AutoPrePlay/AutoPostPlay half of it is turn_structure's G8; neither is re-verdicted here per binding rule 3, but see this record's Mayhem guard for the executed consequence.

guards.rationale:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-07-26 (potion-scope re-verdict pass), from waiver. The shared contract's 'Out of scope everywhere: potions (deferred by Perry)' has been DELETED on Perry's instruction ("don't ignore potions anymore"). `potion` is now an ordinary audit kind -- 51 sim units, audit/records/potion/, `harness.py roster potion` -- and it is UNAUDITED, exactly like `monster`. The previous pass had already narrowed this guard until the only thing left standing on the clause was 'there is no audit/records/potion/ tier for this potion to live in'. That sentence is no longer a scope statement, it is a coverage statement, and coverage is not a waiver. So the guard is re-derived on its merits: the applier potion is read in full against its C# model and verdicted here.
THE APPLIER IS FAITHFUL, INCLUDING ITS INTERNAL ORDER. src/Core/Models/Potions/Clarity.cs:23-27 declares two vars, new PowerVar<ClarityPower>(3m) and new CardsVar(1), with no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 3 and 1 are the pinned non-ascension values; sts2_rl/potions.py:769-770 pins CARDS = 1 and CLARITY = 3. The ORDER is load-bearing and correct: Clarity.cs:33 draws FIRST and Clarity.cs:34 applies the power SECOND, so the immediate card is not itself boosted by the power that was just applied -- sts2_rl/potions.py:775-778 keeps that order (DrawCmd.draw then PowerCmd.apply). Reversing it would draw one extra card on turn 1. APPLIER: C#'s fourth argument to PowerCmd.Apply is `base.Owner.Creature` (src/Core/Commands/PowerCmd.cs:101 declares that parameter as `Creature? applier`), matching the sim's `applier=ctx.player`. TargetType.AnyPlayer (Clarity.cs:21) and AssertValidForTargetedPotion (Clarity.cs:31) are the multiplayer target-validity path, waived as multiplayer; NCombatRoom.PlaySplashVfx (Clarity.cs:32) is presentation. REACHABILITY IS ESTABLISHED, NOT WAIVED (binding rule 6): @register_potion puts it in ALL_POTIONS and it is in the generation pool at sts2_rl/potion_pools.py:44 (uncommon); the conformance runner asserts the belt slot by slot (sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:625-631). WHAT IS STILL NOT JUDGED HERE is a coverage fact, not a verdict: `potion/clarity` has no record yet because the whole potion kind is unaudited. Nothing in this record depends on it.
